content:
iPhone 18 Pro is about to be released, with reports indicating that the Pro Max model may have unique advantages in one or two key areas this year. Here is a summary of what to expect.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will see a significant battery life boost this year, and may also enjoy advantages in the camera department.

Apple's Pro lineup features have remained largely consistent across the years.

Beyond the Pro Max's usual obvious advantage — a larger display and longer battery life — it also occasionally gets exclusive access to a particular camera feature.

This year's rumours around the iPhone 18 Pro suggest that Apple will continue with this approach.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has always been expected to offer better battery life than the iPhone 18 Pro. But based on information recently leaked from regulatory filings, the difference appears set to be more pronounced than ever.

Here's an overview of the leaked battery capacities compared to last year's specs (eSIM versions):

  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 5567mAh
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 4288mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: 5088mAh
  • iPhone 17 Pro: 4252mAh

From this, we can see that the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a battery capacity roughly 10% larger than its predecessor. As for the iPhone 18 Pro's battery, it will be almost identical to the iPhone 17 Pro.

Both new models should benefit from the improved efficiency of the A20 Pro processor and C2 modem, delivering better battery life. However, if you're still weighing up which one to choose, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's battery advantage will be more significant than usual.

One drawback of a larger battery is that the device will also be heavier relative to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Another possible difference involves the camera. Ideally, both Pro models would offer the same feature set. But last autumn, a reputable leaker mentioned that the upcoming variable aperture system might be exclusive to the Pro Max.

This has yet to be confirmed by other sources. However, Mark Gurman has said this year will see particularly significant camera upgrades, so Apple could indeed reserve at least one change for the larger, more expensive model.

Are you a Pro or Pro Max user? What differentiating features might change your choice? Let us know in the comments.
